requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec: `slug` unique 'entities_slug_unique' + softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:17-19); FKs cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', `owner_seq` storedAs "CASE WHEN role = 'owner' THEN 1 END" and unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' / 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-25). Entity has getRouteKeyName()='slug', memberships(), users(), owner() as a HasMany query (Entity.php:22-51). EntityMembership has the UserRole cast, #[Scope] owner/admin/employee, entity()/user() (EntityMembership.php:21-70). UserRole::manageable() returns [Admin, Employee] (UserRole.php:17-20). User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (User.php:34-53). Factories and states are present. Policy rules match the task, including owner-membership deletion denied first and then self-removal (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:26-35). docs/database-schema.md drops owner_membership_id as the task asked.

conventions.evidence: Authorization goes through auto-discovered policies. `#[Fillable]` is set deliberately on both models, using the same attribute style as User. Migrations have generated-style timestamps and reversible down(). Docs and CHANGELOG are updated under [Unreleased]. Pest tests ship with the change. Small deviation: public `isOwner()` (EntityMembership.php:72-75) has no PHPDoc and no test, and nothing uses it.

security.evidence: Every policy check resolves the actor's own membership on the target entity_id (`$user->membershipFor($membership->entity_id)`), so a membership in another entity grants nothing (tested in EntityPolicyTest.php 'membership of another entity grants nothing'). Owner membership deletion is denied before the self-removal branch. Mass assignment is restricted with #[Fillable]. The DB enforces a single owner. No UI or input surfaces were added.

tests.evidence: EntityModelTest covers factories, the slug route key, soft deletes, slug uniqueness, the DB default role, scopes, relations including owner()->first() being null and then set, membershipFor (hit and miss), the duplicate-member rejection, second-owner rejection, multiple owners across entities, owner_seq values, cascade, and the named indexes. EntityPolicyTest uses datasets to cover all four actors for every ability, cross-entity denial, every delete branch and gate discovery. Minor: `toBe(1)` on owner_seq may be driver-type sensitive (string vs int on MariaDB).

simplicity.evidence: Lean code. The policies share one private isOwnerOrAdmin helper each. owner() reuses memberships(). The factory states are one-liners. There are no extra layers or Actions, which is right because the task adds no writes.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods, with short PHPDoc where the intent is non-obvious (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:21-24). In tests, entityWithRoles() returns an array mixing positional and string keys (`$set[0]` for the entity, EntityPolicyTest.php:17-23), which is a bit awkward. It is also a global function declared in a test file. isOwner() is unused.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task: models, migrations, factories, policies, tests, schema doc and changelog. No routes, session, UI or translations were added. Two small extras: an unrequested `isOwner()` helper, and edits to an existing CHANGELOG bullet (removing the 'circular FK note for owner' text) plus removal of `locale_default` from the schema proposal. Both are defensible doc syncs but go a bit beyond the task.

issues.explanation: The public `isOwner()` helper is not part of the contract, nothing uses it, and no test covers it, which goes against 'no production code without a test'.

`expect($seq($owner))->toBe(1)` is a strict-type assertion that can fail on MariaDB/MySQL drivers that return generated integer columns as strings; `toEqual(1)` or an int cast would make the test portable as the task requires.
Dropping `locale_default` from the schema proposal and rewriting an existing changelog bullet go slightly beyond replacing the owner_membership_id design.
The global helper returns an array mixing positional `[0]` and named keys; a named 'entity' key would read better and avoid a global-function collision across test files.

review.summary: The change adds the entities and entity_memberships migrations, including a portable owner_seq generated column with a unique index for the single-owner rule. It also adds the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole models, the User relations, factories, both policies, thorough Pest tests and synced docs/CHANGELOG. Every requirement and contract item is met and authorization is correctly scoped per entity. Only minor issues keep it from a clean approve: an unused, untested isOwner() helper, a driver-sensitive strict assertion, and small doc edits beyond the task.
